correctness.rationale: Deleting one copy of each prescribed part is a bijection onto partitions of the remaining integer; when r+s>n the joint event is impossible and the positive marginals give strict negative covariance. Otherwise, with a=n−r−s, the sign is the opposite of F=p(a+r)p(a+s)−p(a)p(a+r+s). For Q_t(x)=p(x+t)/p(x), products of consecutive ratios show Q_t strictly decreases on x≥26. DeSalvo–Pak Theorem 1.1 is worded as log-concavity, rather than explicitly as strict log-concavity; their Proposition 2.4 proves a positive logarithmic defect for m≥2600. The finite strictness bridge for m=26,…,2599 was independently confirmed in exact arithmetic (minimum integer defect 3052), so the strict premise used in the frozen proof holds. Thus F>0 if a≥26. At smaller a cap both coordinates at R=26−a. Extending s from R increases the normalized difference Q_r(a)−Q_r(a+s), and the analogous normalization works for extending r, so positivity propagates from the caps. If the two caps coincide one uses the positive diagonal defect, not a covariance of a variable with itself. For distinct caps any saturated comparison is strictly positive except a=0,r=1; that exceptional trajectory has F=p(s)−p(s+1)<0 by the part-one insertion map and the missing one-part partition. The independent pentagonal-recurrence replay reproduces all 2,925 distinct-size comparisons, all 26 positive diagonal caps, and all 325 saturated comparisons, with no saturated zero. It yields exactly 11 exceptional positives outside the persistent family and the five zeros, with largest nonpersistent positive n=16. The cap argument, not finite extrapolation, certifies the remaining n.
residual_risks: The unbounded step relies on the published analytic tail estimate; it is not re-proved by the finite replay. The proof only concerns two distinct occurrence indicators.

originality.rationale: Credit Bessenrodt–Ono for the whole a=0, r,s≥2 row (four positive boundary exceptions and three zeros in this parameterization), the elementary insertion argument for the r=1 boundary, and DeSalvo–Pak for the tail. The supported distinct result is the complete off-diagonal finite-size classification, in particular the a>0 mixed-defect sign diagram with seven positive and two zero exceptions. Neither the nearest occurrence/multiplicity works nor the exact known partition inequalities imply that classification without the mixed-shift cap argument and exact finite data.

value.rationale: Presence is a natural observable distinct from multiplicity. Conditioning on total size does not force pairwise negative occurrence dependence: the theorem isolates an infinite positive boundary family and determines the exact last positive away from it. The sharp cutoff at 17 and the equality cases give a concrete benchmark for dependence claims under fixed-total sampling, including when a negative-correlation heuristic is wrong.
residual_risks: No general negative association or classification for more than two indicators, restricted partitions, or alternate sampling laws.
